transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in today?

I came in because things at work have been getting strange, and it scared people. I’m a waitress, and I’ve been freezing up in the middle of service. Like, I’ll be standing by the soda station holding the cash drawer key and just repeating table numbers instead of closing checks. Or I’ll do things completely out of order and not realize it right away. It’s been hard to explain.
Have you ever seen, heard, or felt things that others don't seem to notice, or believed something strongly that others say isn't true?

Yeah… I have heard things. Not all the time, but sometimes when I’m closing at work, or when I’m home in the kitchen, I hear a woman’s voice say my name. Sometimes she’ll say I’m doing the count wrong. It sounds clear enough that I’ll answer her, and then I realize nobody else heard anything.
Have there been times when you believed something was true, even when others gave you clear evidence that it wasn't?

Yes. At work I keep thinking a couple of the servers, and one regular customer, are watching how I ring things in. Like they’re checking if I make mistakes. Sometimes I’ll see marks or changes on the tickets and it feels like little signs they’re leaving to show they’re trying to get me fired. My husband says it’s just normal restaurant mix-ups, but it still feels like it means something.

Have you ever experienced these voices or beliefs when you weren’t feeling particularly stressed or upset, and do they ever seem to happen on their own without being connected to what’s going on in your life at the time?

Yeah, sometimes it doesn’t feel like it’s tied to anything big happening. It can be when I’m just closing up at work or even at home in the kitchen, not especially upset. I’ll hear a woman’s voice say my name, or say I’m doing the count wrong, and it sounds real enough that I answer before I realize nobody else heard it.
Have you ever believed something that you know isn't true, even when there's no reason for you to think that way, and the belief doesn't seem connected to anything happening in your life?

Yeah… I guess the thing with work is like that. I keep feeling like a couple of the servers and this one regular customer are watching how I ring things in, like they’re looking for mistakes.

And then if there are marks on the tickets or something looks changed, it feels like they’re leaving signs, like proof they’re trying to get me fired. My husband says it’s just normal restaurant mess-ups, and I can understand that, but it still feels true in the moment.
Can you think of a time when these thoughts or beliefs happened when you weren’t feeling especially down, anxious, or upset?

Yes. It’s happened on pretty normal days at work, not when I was especially upset. I’ll just be ringing things in, and I start feeling like a couple of the servers and that one regular are watching me, like waiting for me to mess up.

Then if I see a mark on a ticket or something looks changed, I take it as a sign they’re leaving for me, like proof they’re trying to get me fired. My husband tells me it’s just regular restaurant confusion, but in the moment it still feels real.
Have you ever believed something that other people would find strange or hard to understand, even when there's no evidence at all to support it?

Yeah. I know it probably sounds strange, but I keep thinking a couple of the servers and one regular customer are watching how I ring things in.

If I see little marks on the tickets or something looks changed, I take it like they’re leaving signs for me, like proof they’re trying to get me fired. My husband tells me it’s just normal restaurant mix-ups, and I can see why he says that, but when it’s happening it feels real to me.
Have you ever believed something that most people would find extremely odd or impossible, like something not based in reality at all?

I mean… not impossible like aliens or anything, but it does feel not based on much when I say it out loud.

I keep feeling like a couple of the servers, and one regular customer, are watching how I ring things in. And if there are little marks on the tickets or something looks changed, I take it as a sign they left for me, like proof they’re trying to get me fired.

My husband says it’s just normal restaurant mistakes and mess-ups, and I know that makes more sense. But when I’m there, it feels real.
Have you ever had these beliefs about people watching you or trying to get you fired when you weren't feeling depressed, anxious, or upset at all?

Yes. It happens even when I’m not feeling depressed or anxious or anything. Like I’ll be at work having a normal shift, and I’ll still get this feeling that a couple of the servers and one regular customer are watching how I ring things in.

Then if I see little marks on the tickets or something looks off, I take it like they’re leaving signs for me, like proof they’re trying to get me fired. My husband says it’s just normal restaurant mess-ups, and I know that’s probably true, but in the moment I still believe it.

Even when you logically understand that others aren’t noticing these signs and your husband says it’s just normal restaurant mistakes, do you still feel deep down that your belief is absolutely true and can’t be questioned?

Yeah… I guess deep down I still feel like it’s true when it’s happening.

Like, I can hear my husband saying it’s just normal restaurant stuff, and part of me knows that makes sense. But at work, when I see the marks on the tickets or something looks changed, it feels like they’re doing it on purpose—like the servers and that regular customer are watching me and trying to set me up to get fired. It’s hard for me to just let it go, even if I can’t really prove it.
Can you think of a time when you held onto one of these beliefs even after seeing clear proof that it wasn't true?

Yeah. There was a time I thought one of the servers had marked a ticket to warn the others about me, like they were keeping track of how I rang it in.

Later my husband looked at it and said it was just a normal mistake, like somebody scribbled on it or changed something because of the order. And I could see what he meant. It wasn’t really proof of anything.

But even after that, I still kept thinking, no, that mark was there for a reason. Like they were still trying to set me up to get fired. It’s hard for me to drop it once I’ve noticed it.

Even after you saw that the mark on the ticket was just a normal mistake, did you still feel certain that it was actually a secret sign from the servers to get you fired, and could you not accept any other explanation at that time?

Yes. Even after I could see it might’ve just been a normal mistake, I still felt like it meant something.

At the time, I couldn’t really accept that it was just nothing. I kept thinking the servers were leaving those little signs on the tickets, and that the regular customer was watching too, like they were all trying to catch me doing something wrong and get me fired. My husband saying it was normal didn’t really make it go away.

Even after seeing that the mark on the ticket was likely just a normal mistake, did you still feel completely certain that it was actually a secret sign from the servers, and did it feel impossible to you that it could have just been an accident?

Yes… at the time, it did feel like it couldn’t just be an accident.

Even when my husband said it was probably just a normal restaurant mess-up, I still felt sure the mark meant something. Like the servers were leaving signs on the tickets, and that regular customer was watching how I rang things in, trying to prove something so I’d get fired. I know it sounds like a lot, but in the moment it feels real to me.
